column1: # Creative / media. Included only when $PROFILE is desktop; --no-creative opts out.
# NB: this file used to be DaVinci Resolve and a 229-line script to make it work.
# Both are gone, and the reasoning is worth keeping so nobody re-adds them:
#   1. Free Resolve on Linux cannot decode OR encode H.264/H.265 at all - a
#      licensing limit, not a bug. Phone video and screen recordings simply do
#      not import without transcoding every clip first.
#   2. AMD dropped Polaris/gfx803 from ROCm after 5.7 and the repos ship 7.x,
#      which enumerates no OpenCL device on an RX 570 - so Resolve would not
#      even start without pinning four packages to a 2023 release out of the
#      Arch archive and holding them there with IgnorePkg, forever.
# Kdenlive goes through ffmpeg, handles H.264/H.265 natively, and decodes on the
# GPU through VA-API - which the shared "GPU & display stack" doctor step already
# verifies, so it needs no checks of its own.
# NB: Affinity is gone too. It has no Linux build; it ran under Wine, needed its
# own installers and a GUI, and could never be part of a non-interactive
# bootstrap. Canva in the browser replaced it. The Wine rows in gaming.tsv stay -
# Lutris needs them - but they are no longer justified by Affinity.
#id
kdenlive
